newsitem.title: CANADA: DBRS confirms Laurentian Bank ratings.
newsitem.headline: DBRS confirms Laurentian Bank ratings.

text.p: Dominion Bond Rating Service said on Monday it confirmed the ratings for Laurentian Bank of Canada following Laurentian's acquisition of Trust Pret et Revenue in 1996.

DBRS said it confirmed Laurentian's deposits and senior debt at A, subordinated debentures at A(low), cumulative preferred shares (series 2) at Pfd-2, non-cumulative preferred shares (series 6,7,8) at Pfd-2(low) and short-term instruments at R-1(low), all with a stable trend.

The Trust Pret et Revenu acquisition is the tenth for Laurentian in less than seven years, DBRS said. It said with the deal, together with the North American Trust acquisition, Laurentian is rapidly diversifying its sources of non-interest revenue.
DBRS said with the benefit of these two acquisitions, 1996 core earnings increased 26 percent to C$51.7 million while profit was up 53 percent, including non-recurring items.
Past acquisitions have generally helped to further diversify Laurentian's the loan portfolio outside the province of Quebec, DBRS said.

"Despite high commerical real estate exposure, overall asset quality is respectable and continues to gradually improve. While the tier I capital ratio is strong relative to the peer group, excluding (lower quality) preferred equity the ratio is below the industry, but this appears manageable," DBRS said.
Laurentian is 57.5-percent controlled by the Desjardins-Laurentian Financial Corp, providing potential assistance, but no guarantee, DBRS said.
